text:
**1. Summarize how the game went from your perspective**

I started with a fairly standard Catalyst opening: build a credit base with Smartware Distributor, DZMZ Optimizers and Verbal Plasticity, and try to get icebreakers online. Early on I got Carmen and Conduit out, and later installed a second Carmen. The Corp protected HQ with rezzed Karunā + Diviner and R&D with rezzed Diviner + Whitespace, both net-damage heavy. I tried to run HQ with Docklands Pass and Jailbreak on R&D for extra accesses, but Diviner’s net damage and Whitespace’s credit loss / run-end forced a jack out. I never got a Fracter online — Cleaver stayed in heap — so the third ice on Remote 0 and the hidden R&D ice remained unbreakable.

Credit management was tight. I leaned on Smartware Distributor, Creative Commission and Sure Gamble style economy, and installed Unity late in turn 19 to get a Decoder. By then the Corp was already on 4-6 agenda points. On Corp turn 18 they scored the second Offworld Office, jumping to 6 points. On Corp turn 19 they advanced the remote twice. On my turn 19 I installed Unity, put credits on Smartware, then ran HQ into Karunā, took 2 net damage, trashed Telework Contract and Wildcat Strike, and jacked out. I drew once more, and the game ended on Corp turn 20 when they advanced three times and scored Send a Message, reaching 7 agenda points. I finished on 2 points with Orbital Superiority stolen.

**2. What was your plan, and how did it change as the game developed?**

Initial plan: establish economy with Smartware Distributor + Verbal Plasticity for draws, get Killer + Decoder + Fracter online, and use Docklands Pass + Jailbreak to dig HQ/R&D for agendas. I wanted to pressure centrals early before the remote got too big.

As the game developed the plan shifted to survival and credit accumulation. The Corp’s ice suite was net damage focused: Karunā and Diviner both force discards. That made runs very costly. I pivoted to building a credit pool on Smartware and saving clicks for draws, hoping to find Unity/Cleaver. I also tried to keep hand size up to absorb net damage. When the remote was advanced to 2 counters and then 2 more on turn 19, the threat of a 3-point score became urgent, but I lacked a Fracter to touch it.

**3. Key turning points**

* Corp scoring Offworld Office on turn 18 to 6 agenda points, putting the win within one score.
* The failed R&D run with Jailbreak on turn 18: Diviner net damage trashed Smartware Distributor and Whitespace’s “Runner loses 3c / end run if ≤6c” ended the run before breach, costing cards and tempo.
* HQ run into Karunā on turn 19: first subroutine dealt 2 net damage, forcing discards of Telework Contract and Wildcat Strike, then I jacked out. That burned my last offensive window and left me with only 1 credit and 1 click.
* Corp’s turn 20 triple advance and scoring of Send a Message — the game ended before I could draw into a Fracter or a run event.

**4. What I would do differently**

* Prioritise the Decoder earlier. Unity was installed on turn 19 after the Corp already had scoring momentum. Getting a Decoder by turn 15-16 would have let me break Diviner/Whitespace reliably and attempt a central run before the remote was protected.
* Preserve hand size vs net damage. I discarded into damage unnecessarily; keeping cheaper, even-cost cards in grip would have avoided Diviner’s “end the run if odd cost trashed” trigger and reduced net-damage losses.
* Use economy more efficiently. I spent clicks placing credits on Smartware while my credit pool was near zero, which left me unable to pay for breaker strength increases during encounters. A Sure Gamble earlier or keeping a credit buffer would have helped.
* Consider a more aggressive early run on the remote. With three hidden ice pieces, it looked dangerous, but the Corp was advancing aggressively; an early peek with Tread Lightly or Overclock might have forced them to rez and slow down.

**5. Interface / rules presentation**

* The “Run Subroutines” and “Run: Movement” phases made it clear when I could jack out, but the net-damage resolution order and the fact that Smartware Distributor was trashed by Diviner’s damage before I saw the card was confusing at first.
* Counter visibility was helpful: advancement counters on the remote root were public even while the card was hidden, which correctly signaled threat level.
* The discard step selection UI was fine, but having multiple identical options e.g., two Wildcat Strikes with same label made it hard to differentiate copies.
* No major hindrance, though the log compaction at the end made it harder to reconstruct the exact sequence of the final Corp advance/score.

Overall, the game was lost on tempo and breaker coverage; the Corp’s net-damage wall and rapid remote scoring outpaced my ability to assemble a full rig in time.
